summary: Incremental acceptance of 1f1e769e against prior accepted 553d894. The exact-SHA author binding is sound and fail-closed: direct_author_subject records {author, sha} only when LEAD equals the pinned unit author (via checks on direct units, or automatically at review from the author chat); any other lead passes only on strict dict equality with the current rev-parse HEAD, so a moved HEAD (including a coordinator's own commits) is refused before any paid model call, and a non-author checks run never rebinds (regression asserts the record is unchanged and review exits 2 with zero calls). Author/reviewer assignments are untouched, cand_mode units are excluded from binding, protected units keep the symmetric direct-only path, and the original opposite-service reviewer is unchanged, so independence is preserved. Persistence is safe: binding writes go through Task.save/merge_state under state_lock (unit-level three-way merge refuses concurrent double edits rather than clobbering); _do_review syncs before comparing, so a fresh handoff record is visible to the coordinator; absence of the key in legacy/normalize_state and any corrupted non-dict value compare unequal and block (check_state's trusted-local threat model is explicitly unchanged). Checks caching/recovery interact correctly: a red bound SHA stores checks and blocks model review without consuming budget; UNCERTAIN re-review and cached PASS retrieval work for the handed-off coordinator at the same SHA; acceptance still re-verifies reviewed-SHA ancestry and empty unit diff, so post-binding commits invalidate acceptance. Binding on a blocked checks run does not occur (apply_checks raises first), but that state blocks review for everyone anyway, and waive-then-checks binds correctly. The prior MINOR (waive guidance for all-unconfigured classes) is addressed by the explicit SKILL.md paragraph plus a waiver regression, though the test exercises only a single touched class. No BLOCKER/MAJOR found; three MINOR guidance/coverage items reported. Unchanged executable code remains covered by the prior accepted SHA.

findings.problem: test_all_unconfigured_classes_can_be_waived commits only frontend/src/App.tsx, so check_kinds yields a single class and the len(kinds)>1 missing-suite pre-check from the prior finding is never exercised. The exact prior scenario (all touched classes unconfigured, multi-class) still has no regression, and the run_checks blocker wording in that path still omits the waive option; only the new SKILL.md paragraph compensates.
findings.scenario: Fresh baseline with config={}; a direct unit touches both a .py and a .tsx file. checks hits the multi-class pre-check whose closing clause reads as prohibiting waiver; the lead relies solely on SKILL.md to know waive is valid. A future edit to the pre-check or waiver_valid could silently break this path without any failing test, since the new test covers only the single-class branch.
findings.fix: Extend the regression to commit one backend and one frontend file under config={}, assert checks exits 2, then waive succeeds and checks reports waived (mirroring the single-class test). Optionally also assert the blocker text mentions the waiver exit when no class is configured, per the prior review's suggested wording branch.

findings.problem: cmd_checks records direct_author for whatever HEAD currently is, and the binding side effect is not announced distinctly in the output (only the generic 'Проверки <uid> на <sha>' line). The record attests that the author chat endorsed the current HEAD, not that every commit in base..HEAD was written by the author; commits made by another chat since the author's last commit are silently included in the endorsement.
findings.scenario: Reviewer-lead chat commits directly to unit files (against the process rule) or unrelated commits land on the branch; the author chat later runs checks as a routine recovery step after an environment blocker. The combined HEAD is bound, and the opposite service then reviews a range that includes its own chat's commits. Exposure is comparable to the old author-runs-review flow and the trusted-local model excludes adversarial leads, but checks is a cheaper, more routine command, so blind endorsement is easier; the author gets no explicit signal that a handoff fixation was just written.
findings.fix: In cmd_checks, when the binding is recorded, print an explicit line such as 'Авторская фиксация: <author> <sha> — этот SHA может отправить на review любой координатор', and add one sentence to SKILL.md step 3 that the author must verify HEAD is exactly their intended submission before running checks for handoff.

findings.problem: The _do_review refusal message for a SHA mismatch does not include the recorded bound SHA and only directs the coordinator back to the author's checks command. When HEAD merely moved (e.g., the coordinator's checkout is at a different commit, or unrelated commits landed) while a valid binding exists, the message misdirects: checking out the already-bound SHA would suffice, no new author fixation is needed.
findings.scenario: Author binds SHA X via checks and hands off. The coordinator chat's HEAD is at X plus an unrelated commit outside the unit's files (or a different branch position). review exits 2 telling them the author must run checks again; the coordinator bounces the unit back to the author chat for a cheap re-bind (or re-checkout) that they could have resolved themselves by checking out X. Fail-closed and recoverable, but the handoff round-trip is unnecessary and the error text asserts 'Новый SHA требует новой авторской фиксации' even when the current SHA is not new work.
findings.fix: Include the stored binding in the need() message when present, e.g. 'зафиксирован <author> <sha[:10]>; текущий HEAD <tip[:10]> — переключись на зафиксированный SHA либо попроси автора выполнить checks на новом HEAD'. Keep the existing author-checks instruction when no binding exists.
